rfi.description: A year after paramilitary forces at war with the Sudanese army captured the strategic city of El Fasher, survivors and aid workers report that the capital of North Darfur state remains largely abandoned. Some residents are too scared to return, while thousands are still missing – many held in deplorable conditions in overcrowded prisons.

rfi.description: How do you report on the reality of a Russia at war from its capital? Based in Moscow for more than 30 years, the BBC's Russia correspondent Steve Rosenberg is one of the few Western journalists still working in the country. He spoke to RFI about his daily life as a reporter in Russia and why he has chosen to stay, despite the Kremlin's increasing hostility to foreign media.

rfi.title: 'Protecting the Congo's forests means protecting people's lives'
rfi.description: The forests of eastern Democratic Republic of Congo are a haven for some of the world's rarest species – but despite being protected areas, they are under threat from conflict, poaching and deforestation. After global decision-makers gathered at the United Nations' Cop17 biodiversity summit this week, Emmanuel Bahati Lukoo, a ranger at Kahuzi-Biega National Park, says people on the frontline of wildlife protection deserve greater recognition.

rfi.description: For Ukrainian media, exposing corruption in times of war is a high-stakes move – with domestic scandals potentially tarnishing the country's image in the eyes of the international partners it relies on. But journalists remain dedicated to their role as a counterbalance to the authorities, believing that upholding democracy is more important now than ever.

rfi.title: 'African leaders are not naive, they will partner with whoever makes the best offer’
rfi.description: The third Russia-Africa Summit took place in Moscow this week, with 48 African nations sending delegations. It comes as Moscow grapples with sanctions and isolation over its Ukraine offensive, while African governments turn to it for security assistance. However, geopolitical analyst Priyal Singh tells RFI that despite this, Russia still lags behind China in its influence on the continent.

rfi.title: France sees third weekend of protests as youth-led rallies sweep Europe
rfi.description: Hundreds of thousands of mostly young protesters, some dressed as clowns and witches for Halloween, took to the streets across France on Saturday in a third weekend of demonstrations over living costs and education. Police fired tear gas in Paris after clashes broke out at the end of the march. Youth rallies were also held in Germany and Italy.

rfi.title: Can Latino discontent loosen Republican grip on Florida?
rfi.description: Rising petrol prices and anger over immigration raids are testing Latino support for Republicans in Florida. Ahead of Tuesday’s midterm elections, Democrats see an opening in a state that has swung firmly to the right, but economic frustration may not be enough to overturn years of Republican dominance.

Une rencontre du théâtre et de l’histoire pour aider la haute administration à examiner son passé mais, aussi, ses responsabilités présentes.

france24fr.title: Présidentielle 2027 : la primaire de la droite et du centre n'aura pas lieu
france24fr.description:
Au menu de Présidentielle 2027 : une nouvelle semaine de mobilisation sociale avec le blocage des lycées et la grève du 5 novembre. On évoque aussi la primaire de la droite et du centre voulue par le candidat Gabriel Attal, mais à laquelle Natacha Polony et Edouard Philippe viennent d'opposer une fin de non-recevoir.
 
Avec Philippe Moreau-Chevrolet, Président de MCBG Conseil et soutien de Gabriel Attal, et Stéphane Vernay, éditorialiste politique et Rédacteur en chef délégué chez Ouest-France.

france24fr.title: A table avec Coline Doussin, cheffe patissière du Saint James Paris
france24fr.description: A l'occasion de la 31ème édition du Salon du chocolat à Paris, la cheffe patissière du Saint James Paris, Coline Doussin, est venue nous présenter ses dernières créations.

france24fr.title: Pourquoi le vote arabo-musulman pourrait compter au Michigan
france24fr.description: Aux États-Unis, la communauté arabe et musulmane est appelée à voter à travers tout le Michigan pour les élections de mi-mandat. Ses membres, souvent de fervents soutiens du candidat démocrate Abdul el-Sayed, sont très critiques du président américain Donald Trump et de sa politique au Moyen-Orient. De Dearborn, "capitale arabe d'Amérique du Nord", à Warren, notre journaliste Valentin Cacheux est allé à la rencontre de cette minorité qui pourrait peser lourd dans le scrutin des midterms 2026.

france24fr.title: Jean-Pierre Filiu : "Gaza est un laboratoire pour l'ensemble du système international"
france24fr.description: Un an après la proclamation d'un cessez-le-feu dans la bande de Gaza, l'enclave est toujours largement occupée par l'armée israélienne, les bombardements quotidiens et meurtriers, et les conditions de vie extrêmes. C'est dans ce contexte de tragédie continue au Proche-Orient que se sont tenues les premières élections législatives en Israël depuis le 7 octobre 2023. L'historien Jean Pierre Filiu, auteur de "L' Étrange aveuglement" (éditions les Arènes), était l'invité d'Au Cœur de l'Info.

france24fr.title: Présidentielle 2027 : Édouard Philippe refuse de participer à une primaire, source de "division"
france24fr.description: Le candidat Horizons à l'élection présidentielle, Édouard Philippe, a confirmé dimanche son refus de participer à une éventuelle primaire de la droite et du centre. L'idée d'une "primaire des démocrates" a été proposée par son concurrent Gabriel Attal dans le but, selon lui, d'empêcher que le second tour oppose LFI au RN.

france24fr.title: Ukraine : à la fin de la trêve à Olechky, la population se prépare à une reprise de la guerre
france24fr.description: La trêve exceptionnelle débutée mardi à Olechky a pris fin dimanche soir, Moscou ayant refusé une proposition de l'Ukraine de prolonger ce cessez-le-feu. Sur place, les autorités saluent le respect de l'accord mais s'attendent à une reprise immédiate et violente de la guerre.

france24fr.title: JOJ Dakar 2026 : les coulisses de l'édition spéciale du dimanche
france24fr.description: JOJ Dakar 2026 🇸🇳 Les coulisses de l'édition spéciale du Journal de l'Afrique. Médailles et temps forts des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse : rendez-vous dimanche à 21h42 (Paris), 20h42 à Dakar, avec Fatimata Wane sur France 24 📺

france24fr.title: Allemagne : plusieurs partis condamnent les violences et appellent à écouter la "Gen Z"
france24fr.description: Des responsables politiques des Verts et de la gauche radicale ont affirmé leur soutien, dimanche, à la jeunesse, tout en condamnant les violences survenues en marge des manifestations samedi. Le gouvernement a de son côté accusé "des groupes de gauche enclins à la violence" d'être responsables des débordements.

france24fr.title: Départ de la 13e Route du Rhum sous une "très belle journée ensoleillée"
france24fr.description: Les 115 marins engagés sur la Route du Rhum se sont lancés dimanche, au large de Saint-Malo dans des conditions météo clémentes, à l'assaut de l'Atlantique, pour une traversée en solitaire que les plus rapides pourraient effectuer en un temps record. Cédric Ferreira était là lors du départ, il nous en dit plus.

france24fr.title: Pologne : pourquoi ce bras de fer entre Tusk et Nawrocki ?
france24fr.description: La Commission européenne a pris le parti du Premier ministre polonais Donald Tusk samedi 31 octobre en appelant le président polonais Karol Nawrocki à valider la nomination de juges pour dénouer une profonde crise politique à Varsovie. Nous en parlons avec notre journaliste en plateau Mélina Huet.

france24fr.title: JOJ Dakar 2026 : la relève de la boxe féminine kenyane à l'assaut des podiums
france24fr.description: 🇰🇪 Avec la deuxième plus grande délégation des JOJ de Dakar, juste derrière le Sénégal, le Kenya compte sur sa nouvelle génération d’athlètes pour briller. Après avoir terminé en tête des nations africaines à Paris 2024 le pays affiche ses ambitions, notamment en boxe féminine.

france24fr.title: Ukraine : dernier jour d'une trêve exceptionnelle à Olechky
france24fr.description: La trêve qui a permis l'évacuation d'habitants d'Olechky, ville occupée par la Russie dans le sud de l'Ukraine, doit prendre fin dimanche soir, un répit exceptionnel mais circonscrit alors que Kiev et Moscou poursuivent par ailleurs leurs frappes. Nous en parlons avec la journaliste Tetyana Ogarkova, responsable du département international de l'Ukraine Crisis Media Center.

france24fr.title: Inde : des milliers de manifestants contre la révision des listes électorales
france24fr.description: Des milliers de personnes se sont rassemblées dimanche à New Delhi à l'appel des partis d'opposition pour exiger la démission du chef de la Commission électorale à la suite de la révision controversée des listes électorales. Nous en parlons avec notre correspondante Jeanne Hutin.

france24fr.title: Sahara occidental : fin de la mission onusienne
france24fr.description: La mission onusienne chargée depuis 35 ans de veiller au respect du cessez-le-feu de 1991 au Sahara occidental prend fin ce dimanche 1er novembre. Faute d'accord au Conseil de sécurité, sa reconduction n'a pas pu être votée. Le Maroc a salué un pas significatif vers la clôture du dossier et sommé la MINURSO de quitter son territoire.

france24fr.title: Le cessez-le-feu à Olechky a permis aux habitants "de rejoindre l'Ukraine libre"
france24fr.description: La trêve qui a permis l'évacuation d'habitants d'Olechky, ville occupée par la Russie dans le sud de l'Ukraine, doit prendre fin ce dimanche 1er novembre au soir, un répit exceptionnel mais circonscrit alors que Kiev et Moscou poursuivent par ailleurs leurs frappes. Notre correspondante Emmanuelle Chaze nous en dit plus.

france24fr.title: Midterms aux États-Unis : "Trump a décidé d'en faire un référendum"
france24fr.description: La campagne pour les élections de mi-mandat, les "midterms" aux États-Unis, touche à sa fin. Trump aurait pu "glisser" sur ces élections et se dire que de toute façon, le président en exercice les perd toujours, mais "il a décidé d'en faire un référendum", analyse notre invité Romuald Sciora, directeur de l'Observatoire politique et géostratégique des États-Unis de l'IRIS.

france24fr.title: L'ONU officialise la "liquidation" de sa mission au Sahara occidental
france24fr.description: Le mandat de la Mission des Nations unies pour l'organisation d'un référendum au Sahara occidental (MINURSO), mise en place en 1991, n'a pas été renouvelé, a annoncé l'ONU dimanche. Cela fait suite à un veto opposé par la Russie à un projet américain de résolution favorable au plan d'autonomie marocain.

france24fr.title: Midterms aux États-Unis : le coût de la vie au cœur du débat
france24fr.description: À deux jours des élections de mi-mandat aux États-Unis, les réunions publiques s'enchaînent. Le pouvoir d'achat est la principale préoccupation des Américains. Dans le Michigan, près de 40% des habitants ont du mal à payer leurs dépenses du quotidien. Des candidats démocrates promettent de faire baisser le coût de la vie s'ils sont élus.

zeit.title: Erschreckende Funde: Nadeln in Halloween-Süßigkeiten - Was die Behörden nun raten
Zwischenwahlen in den USA: Gericht weist Klage gegen Alaska wegen Kandidatennamen ab
zeit.description: In Alaska konkurrieren zwei Republikaner mit dem gleichen Nachnamen um einen Sitz im Senat. Der US-Präsident befürchtet Stimmverluste und will in die Wahl eingreifen.

zeit.title: Krieg gegen die Ukraine: Gehackte Luftalarm-App warnt vor falschen Gefahren
zeit.description: Ukraines Luftwaffe bestätigt den Hack einer Luftalarm-App, die vor russischen Angriffen warnt. In Oleschky ist die Waffenpause beendet. Das Liveblog

zeit.title: «Gen Z regelt»: Hessens Innenminister: Genehmigung neuer Proteste fraglich
Italiener löst Vettel ab: Pressestimmen zum Antonelli-Titel: Der Bambino-Champion
Leute: Nico Santos steckte mit Tänzern in Hotelaufzug fest
«Durch den Monsun»: Tokio Hotel in Hamburg - Fans erleben große Show
Sexualstrafrecht: Hubig legt Gesetz für härtere Strafen bei sexuellen Übergriffen vor
zeit.description: Ein Gesetzentwurf von Bundesjustizministerin Stefanie Hubig sieht längere Verjährungsfristen für Vergewaltigungen vor. Auch verbale Belästigung soll strafbar werden.

zeit.title: Süßes oder Saures?: Schrauben in Süßigkeiten und illegale Böller zu Halloween
Zwischenwahlen in den USA: Demokratin Stevens unterstützt Republikaner Rogers in Michigan
zeit.description: Haley Stevens hat in Michigan die Vorwahlen der Demokraten gegen Abdul El-Sayed verloren. Vor den Midterms stellt sie sich hinter den republikanischen Kandidaten.

zeit.title: Russischer Angriffskrieg: Radioaktive Strahlung? Ukrainische Notfall-Warnungen gehackt
Tarifverhandlungen: Erste Warnstreiks in der Metallindustrie am Montag
Formel 1: Kimi Antonelli wird jüngster Formel-1-Weltmeister der Geschichte
zeit.description: Dem 20-jährigen Italiener reichte beim Großen Preis von Mexiko-Stadt Platz drei für den vorzeitigen Titelgewinn. Antonelli löst Sebastian Vettel als jüngsten Champion ab.

zeit.title: Cybersicherheit: Digitalminister bestätigt Hackerangriff auf Abgeordnetenhandys
zeit.description: Handys von Abgeordneten wurden laut Bundesdigitalminister Wildberger von Hackern attackiert. Wer hinter dem Angriff steckt, sei bislang unklar.

zeit.title: Gen Z regelt: Pistorius hinterfragt Dobrindts Aussagen über Randalierer
zeit.description: Verteidigungsminister Pistorius hat sich von den Aussagen des Innenministers Dobrindt über Randalierer distanziert. Der SPD-Politiker will zunächst die Fakten prüfen.

spiegel.title: USA: Privatjet stürzt in Wohngebiet in Florida – neun Tote
spiegel.description: Überwachungskameras filmten den Einschlag, ein gewaltiger Krater zeugt von der Wucht: Nahe West Palm Beach ist ein Privatflugzeug abgestürzt. Das Unglück ereignete sich in einer belebten Gegend.

spiegel.title: Formel 1: Kimi Antonelli ist Weltmeister - Reaktionen von Sebastian Vettel und der Presse
spiegel.description: Einen jüngeren Formel-1-Weltmeister gab es nie: Kimi Antonelli ist nach seiner Krönung dankbar und sprachlos. Die Medien in seiner Heimat Italien sind außer sich. Und der bisherige Rekordhalter analysiert den Siegeszug des 20-Jährigen.

spiegel.title: USA: Demokraten in Michigan werfen Haley Stevens nach Eklat offenbar raus
spiegel.description: In Michigan eskaliert der parteiinterne Streit bei den Demokraten: Ex-Anwärterin Haley Stevens schlug sich auf die Seite des politischen Gegners. Das hat nun offenbar drastische Konsequenzen.

spiegel.title: Formel 1: Kimi Antonelli ist jüngster Weltmeister der Geschichte
spiegel.description: Mit 20 Jahren löst der Italiener Kimi Antonelli Sebastian Vettel als jüngsten Champion der Formel-1-Geschichte ab. Beim Großen Preis von Mexiko genügte ihm ein dritter Platz zum vorzeitigen Titelgewinn.

spiegel.title: Blutspenden: DRK warnt vor kritischem Mangel an Blutkonserven
spiegel.description: Notfälle sind weiterhin abgesichert, bei planbaren Operationen könnte es zu Verschiebungen kommen: Die Blutreserven sinken in mehreren Bundesländern unter eine kritische Marke. Das DRK bittet dringend um Blutspenden.

spiegel.title: Israel: Yair Golan warnt vor neuem Krieg mit Iran unter Netanyahu
spiegel.description: Yair Golan hat die Erben der Arbeiterpartei bei der Knessetwahl zu neuen Höhen geführt. Nun warnt der linke Oppositionspolitiker davor, dass die Israelis zum »Werkzeug in Netanyahus Kampf um sein politisches Überleben« werden.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump prahlt neue Angriffsziele in Iran ins Spiel - »Pickaxe Mountain«?
spiegel.description: »Wir müssen uns noch um ein oder zwei Anlagen kümmern, aber das können wir in zehn Minuten erledigen«: Donald Trump spricht über Angriffe auf Iran – auch auf ein Ziel 200 Kilometer südlich von Teheran.

spiegel.title: Ukraine bringt kurz vor Ende der lokalen Waffenruhe fast 200 Zivilisten aus Cherson in Sicherheit
spiegel.description: Es war die längste lokale Unterbrechung der Kämpfe seit Beginn ‌der russischen Großinvasion 2022: Die ukrainische Armee hat Männer, Frauen und Kinder aus bedrohten Gebieten südlich von Cherson evakuiert. Nun endet die Feuerpause.

spiegel.title: BSI warnt: Mögliche Spähsoftware auf iPhones von Politikern
spiegel.description: Das BSI hat Politiker vor möglicher Spähsoftware auf ihren iPhones alarmiert. Digitalminister Wildberger bestätigt den Hinweis, lässt aber offen, wer hinter den Angriffen stecken könnte.

spiegel.title: Alaska: Donald Trump scheitert mit Präventiv-Klage zu Namensvettern Sullivan
spiegel.description: Dan S. Sullivan will für Alaska bei den Midterms punkten – Dan J. Sullivan auch. Jetzt treten sie gegeneinander an und das ist rechtens, auch wenn die Republikaner verlieren.

spiegel.title: Bulgarien: Iliana Jotowa nach Prognosen vorn
spiegel.description: Sie gehört dem russlandfreundlichen Lager in Bulgarien an: Iliana Jotowa wird wohl ihr Amt als Präsidenten behalten. Die Wählerbeteiligung war niedrig.

spiegel.title: Boris Pistorius und die Linke: Rot-Grün-Rot in Berlin? Der beliebteste SPD-Minister ist dagegen
spiegel.description: Zahlreiche prominente Ex-Minister aus den Reihen der SPD warnen vor einem Bündnis mit der Linken in Berlin, darunter Sigmar Gabriel und Karl Lauterbach. Nun schließt sich der beliebteste SPD-Bundesminister ihnen an.

spiegel.title: USA: Streit mit Abdul El-Sayed – Demokratin Haley Stevens wechselt ins Rogers-Lager
spiegel.description: Krasser Seitenwechsel im US-Wahlkampf: Die Demokratin Haley Stevens unterstützt jetzt den Republikaner Mike Rogers. Ihr demokratischer Parteikollege Abdul El-Sayed gibt sich betont gelassen.

spiegel.title: »Im Verhör«: Korrupte Justiz (1): Vom Rechtsanwalt zum Drogenboss - SPIEGEL TV
spiegel.description: Benjamin D. führt jahrelang ein gefährliches Doppelleben. Der Jurist versorgt seine Klienten nicht nur mit strafvereitelnden Ratschlägen, sondern mischt auch selbst im großen Stil bei Drogendeals mit.

spiegel.title: Eintracht Frankfurt: 16-jähriger Niko Iličević stellt Altersrekord gegen HSV auf
spiegel.description: Sein Onkel Ivo spielte einst für den HSV, jetzt schreibt der 16-jährige Niko Iličević beim Sieg gegen die Hamburger Bundesligageschichte. Kein Spieler war bei seinem Debüt jünger.

spiegel.title: Premier League: FC Arsenal beendet Sieglos-Serie bei Liverpool dank Kai Havertz
spiegel.description: Beim letzten Sieg der Gunners in Liverpool traf noch Lukas Podolski: Dank Kai Havertz und einer aufopferungsvollen Abwehr klettert der FC Arsenal wieder an die Tabellenspitze. Liverpool hielt sein Pressing nur eine Halbzeit lang durch.

spiegel.title: A9 in Bayern: Hunderte Nägel und Schrauben auf Fahrbahn – Polizei ermittelt
spiegel.description: Hunderte Nägel, Schrauben und Metallwinkel liegen auf der A9 und beschädigen zahlreiche Autoreifen. Die Polizei vermutet eine gezielte Aktion und sucht nach den Verantwortlichen.

spiegel.title: DFB-Pokal-Ausloung: FC Bayern gegen Hertha BSC, Eintracht Frankfurt vs BVB
spiegel.description: Zu gleich sechs Duellen zwischen Bundesliga und zweiter Liga kommt es im Achtelfinale des DFB-Pokals. Das Spitzenspiel steigt in Frankfurt, wenn die Eintracht auf den BVB trifft.

observador.title: 1h. Acampada Porto. Manifestantes admitem desmobilizar
observador.description: Intenção era pernoitar na Praça D. João I, com tendas, mas, perante chegada da PSP, manifestantes ponderam desistir. Ainda nesta edição, partiu-se a corda: Rui Borges está de saída do Sporting.

observador.title: A coesão social
observador.description: As sociedades cosmopolitas, as fronteiras porosas e a imigração em massa destroem a coesão social e o sentido de pertença que permitem pessoas bem formadas e projetos coletivos efetivos.

observador.title: Psicologia do protesto
observador.description: Manifestações com polícia e violência são, assim, uma luz e uma esperança para esta esquerda: um sinal de que surge alguém capaz de abdicar do conforto que a destruiu.

observador.title: A despesa à inflação, os impostos a metade
observador.description: Quatro anos para baixar os impostos a sério

observador.title: Fertilidade. Movimento quer consulta entre os 20 e 35 anos
observador.description: O Movimento +Fertilidade avança com 15 recomendações estratégicas, incluindo o alargamento do acesso à preservação da fertilidade por razões não médicas.

observador.title: Carta aberta ao Senhor Ministro da Educação
observador.description: A verdade inquestionável é que é o princípio da subsidiariedade do Estado que está expressamente inscrito na nossa Constituição, e não o centralismo

observador.title: Um Orçamento entre demasiadas incertezas
observador.description: Num contexto internacional incerto, acrescentar sucessivamente diminuições de receita ou aumentos permanentes de despesa sem uma visão do seu efeito conjunto é uma forma peculiar de fazer política

observador.title: 00h. Kimi Antonelli campeão do mundo de Formula 1
observador.description: Vitória na Cidade do México. Piloto da Mercedes é o mais jovem campeão da história da modalidade. Ainda, uma centena de pessoas na Praça D. João I com a garantia de que vão pernoitar na praça.

observador.title: Estados Unidos da América
observador.description: O centrão, que hoje se zanga no Parlamento e se entende no Orçamento, nasceu assim: dois partidos incubados no mesmo envelope.

observador.title: O socialismo, e porque não concordo com ele
observador.description: O maior receio do socialista (democrático) nem é tanto perder as eleições. O seu maior receio é que a sociedade seja civil ou seja, que não precise dele.

observador.title: A Nuvem tem chaminé
observador.description: Quatro perguntas sobre um data center: qual a potência pedida à EDA? Quanto vai consumir por ano? De onde vem essa energia, e quem paga a produção e a rede que faltarem? Que ruído vpara os vizinhos?

observador.title: Portugal está em Jogo
observador.description: O jogo e as apostas estão cada vez mais presentes. Entre receitas fiscais, publicidade e patrocínios, estará o Estado a fazer o suficiente para proteger os consumidores?

observador.title: O direito de não achar graça
observador.description: À televisão pública cabe acolher a liberdade artística e ouvir a crítica dos cidadãos. Não se confunda provocação com talento, nem ausência de respeito com coragem.

observador.title: O mal-estar europeu: quando a democracia deixa de prometer
observador.description: O maior risco para a democracia europeia não é apenas a desconfiança nos políticos. É a perda de esperança de que a política ainda possa construir um futuro melhor.

observador.title: Bessent Foi Atrás do Dinheiro Sujo
observador.description: Bruxelas mais uma vez leu desdém por parte da administração Trump. A City de Londres e Wall Street leram nas entrelinhas: convém prestar muita atenção ao que os EUA têm para dizer.

observador.title: As geometrias de poder
observador.description: Que ironia suprema a de um continente que inventou a diplomacia e o próprio conceito de real-politik, e que descobre agora, tarde e a preço de retalho, que o poder nunca foi direito adquirido.

observador.title: As gafarias que escondiam doentes da sociedade em Portugal
observador.description: As gafarias são um testemunho particularmente interessante dessa realidade e permitem compreender como a assistência, a religião e a organização social se cruzavam na Idade Média.

observador.title: Liderança na era da IA
observador.description: A IA pode acelerar decisões e transformar o trabalho. Mas liderar continua a exigir discernimento, coragem e responsabilidade - e a capacidade de mobilizar pessoas num mundo em mudança.

nzz.title: MELDUNGEN POLIZEI - In Teilen von Brugg ist zeitweise der Strom ausgefallen
nzz.description: Die neuesten Polizeimeldungen aus der Schweiz.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Midterms 2026: Gericht weist Trumps Klage zu Wahl in Alaska ab +++ In Michigan stellt sich eine Demokratin auf die Seite des republikanischen Senatskandidaten
nzz.description: Am 3. November wählen die Amerikaner einen neuen Kongress. Bei den Midterms entscheidet sich, ob die Republikaner ihre Mehrheiten im Senat und im Repräsentantenhaus halten können. Alle Entwicklungen im Ticker.

nzz.title: Das Tennismärchen des Valentin Vacherot geht weiter – der Monegasse gewinnt die Swiss Indoors
nzz.description: Vor einem Jahr reüssierte der 27-jährige Spätzünder als Nummer 204 der Welt beim Masters-1000-Turnier in Schanghai. Mit dem Titel in Basel zeigt Vacherot nun, dass dieser Triumph kein Ausreisser war.

nzz.title: DER ANDERE BLICK - Die Gewaltexzesse in deutschen Städten sind ein Angriff auf die westliche Gesellschaft
nzz.description: Der liberale Rechtsstaat allein kann die Attacken der linksextremen und der migrantischen Antikapitalisten gegen die bürgerliche Gesellschaftsordnung nicht abwehren. Er braucht die Unterstützung durch die Politik und vor allem durch das Bürgertum.

nzz.title: BILDSTRECKE - Mexiko feiert den Tag der Toten mit farbenfrohen Paraden
nzz.description: Der traditionelle «Día de Muertos» zählt zu den wichtigsten Feiertagen Mexikos und wurde 2008 von der Unesco in die Liste des immateriellen Kulturerbes aufgenommen. Mit Musik und knalligen Farben wird an mehreren Tagen der Verstorbenen gedacht.

nzz.title: Wie der Raub von mehr als 6 Milliarden Dollar an Krypto-Vermögen ablief. Eine Rekonstruktion
nzz.description: Nordkoreanische Hacker sollen die Attacke auf die Krypto-Börse Binance verübt haben. Wie die Kriminellen dabei vorgingen – und was der Riesendiebstahl für Anleger in Kryptowährungen bedeutet.

nzz.title: Mutterliebe für das Vaterland: Der Ukraine-Krieg erreicht die Opernbühne
nzz.description: Das Musiktheater «Mothers of Kherson» handelt von ukrainischen Müttern, die ihre verschleppten Kinder suchen. Die Koproduktion der Polnischen Nationaloper und der New Yorker Met orientiert sich an realen Schicksalen. Gut gemacht oder bloss gut gemeint?

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Jugendproteste in Europa: Knapp 780 Festnahmen in Frankreich und mindestens 250 in Deutschland +++ Frankfurt erwägt Verbot der nächsten Gen-Z-Demo
nzz.description: In Frankreich und Deutschland haben am Samstag Hunderttausende Jugendliche protestiert. In der Schweiz kam es bei Demonstrationen in Zürich und Basel zu Zwischenfällen.

nzz.title: Die Krawalle waren angekündigt, trotzdem gab es kaum Festnahmen in Zürich. Die Halloween-Taktik der Linksextremen ist aufgegangen
nzz.description: Die Stadtpolizei sieht sich nach den Verwüstungen vom Samstagabend erneut mit der Kritik konfrontiert, nicht hart genug durchzugreifen. Sie kontert, sie habe Schlimmeres verhindern können.

nzz.title: Der FC Zürich feiert einen Spektakel-Sieg und fügt YB die erste Saisonniederlage zu - Lugano nun schon neun Punkte voraus
nzz.description: Die Zürcher brillieren in der zweiten Halbzeit und machen aus einem 2:3 ein 5:3. Umeh Emmanuel gelingen zwei Tore. Weil der FC Lugano gegen Basel mit 2:1 gewinnt, ist sein Vorsprung bereits komfortabel.

nzz.title: «Es kann keinen Kompromiss geben»: Der Machtkampf um das Verfassungsgericht stürzt Polen in eine Krise
nzz.description: Nach den staatsstreichartigen Szenen in Warschau und der Absetzung des Gerichtspräsidenten ist unklar, wie der Streit beigelegt werden kann. Das Verfassungsgericht dürfte auf Dauer handlungsunfähig sein.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Crans-Montana: Mehrere Opfer reichen Aufsichtsbeschwerde gegen die Gemeinde Crans-Montana ein
nzz.description: In der Bar «Le Constellation» in Crans-Montana im Wallis ist es in der Neujahrsnacht zu einem verheerenden Brand gekommen. 41 Personen sind ums Leben gekommen. Die Ermittlungen laufen. Das sind die neuesten Entwicklungen.

nzz.title: MELDUNGEN KULTUR - Filmproduzentin Regina Ziegler mit 82 Jahren gestorben

phys-org.title: Mars dust may be less abrasive than lunar dust, spacesuit samples suggest
phys-org.description: Tucked away among its sensors, cameras and navigation tools, NASA's Mars rover Perseverance is wearing small swatches of spacesuit material. A rover doesn't need a spacesuit, but the swatches—each less than a square inch (6.5 square centimeters) in size—serve an important purpose: They're helping scientists assess the potential damage caused by ubiquitous Martian dust.

phys-org.title: New restrictions kick in as Delhi battles pollution
phys-org.description: Authorities in New Delhi stepped up anti-pollution measures on Sunday, including higher parking fees and work-from-home orders, seeking to curb toxic smog in one of the world's most polluted capitals.

phys-org.title: 'Air-con nation' Singapore eyes alternatives to cool down
phys-org.description: Long dubbed an "air-conditioned nation," Singapore is experimenting with cooling alternatives from chilled beams to "passive displacement" to curb its thirst for energy-guzzling air conditioning.

phys-org.title: From Italy to Croatia, a warming climate threatens prized white truffles
phys-org.description: Guided by the beam of a flashlight, Tino Marolo follows his dog Stella through the darkness of a Piedmont woodland, searching for one of Italy's most prized culinary treasures hidden beneath the soil.

phys-org.title: Warmer seas and shifting pressure systems: The signs that suggest the Mediterranean's climate is 'tropicalizing'
phys-org.description: Nowhere in the Iberian Peninsula or the Balearic Islands has a tropical climate—for this to be the case, the average temperature in the coldest month would have to be 18°C (64 degrees Fahrenheit) or higher. The contrast between Spain's winters and summers, and the low temperatures reached in winter, do not resemble those of any tropical climate.

phys-org.title: Why some trees thrive far from home—and what that means for carbon sinks
phys-org.description: In a study spanning 192 sites and four continents, researchers have discovered that conifers planted in the Southern Hemisphere grow up to four times faster and are more drought-resistant than those growing in their native ranges.

phys-org.title: How permanent daylight saving time could affect schools
phys-org.description: Sleep is fundamental to well-being. Decisions to end semiannual clock changes and remain on permanent daylight saving time (DST) in British Columbia, the Northwest Territories, Alberta, Manitoba and northwestern Ontario have consequences for many Canadians due to potential sleep disruption.

phys-org.title: Heavy hydrogen in 3I/ATLAS's methane points to a frigid birthplace
phys-org.description: The interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS carries a chemical clue to conditions in the planetary system of its origin, locked away long before it reached our sun. Its methane signature is unusually rich in heavy hydrogen, suggesting that the comet's frozen ingredients took shape in an intensely cold environment around another star—or in the cloud that preceded it.

phys-org.title: 2,700-year-old mummy head yields first molecular evidence linking aloe to Egyptian embalming
phys-org.description: What materials did ancient Egyptians use to preserve the dead, and how can their composition still be investigated thousands of years later? An interdisciplinary team at Marburg University has combined modern natural product analysis with Egyptology and the history of pharmacy to investigate these questions.

phys-org.title: Breaking the ice: Scientists use attracting particles to form an anti-spin ice
phys-org.description: In a recent Nature Communications study, researchers have reported the realization of an anti-spin ice, a system that does the opposite of conventional spin ices by breaking the ice rule that governs them.

phys-org.title: This oddball reflective lava world is challenging to understand
phys-org.description: Among Kepler and TESS's many surprising exoplanet discoveries are the ultra-short-period (USP) planets. These planets move very quickly and complete an orbit in less than 24 hours. Ancient astronomers thought that Mercury was so fast—it goes around the sun every 88 days—that they named it after the Roman god Mercury, who was the fast-traveling messenger of the gods. They couldn't have known how sluggish Mercury is compared to the USPs.

phys-org.title: Looking for bats after dark can help science—and change how we see them
phys-org.description: What's that chirping sound coming through the detector? Did you feel something whiz past? Those are just some ways people react when they encounter microbats for the first time. Microbats are small, mostly nocturnal mammals that use ultrasonic sounds to navigate and hunt at night. They do this through echolocation, producing calls and listening to the echoes that bounce back from objects and prey.

phys-org.title: Giant virus yields potassium channel gene that illuminates complex protein evolution
phys-org.description: Researchers have discovered a gene for a tandem potassium channel in an algal virus. The finding supports the view that giant viruses may have contributed significantly to the evolution of complex proteins. The study is published in the journal Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.

phys-org.title: Why do people prefer human empathy despite rating AI empathy higher?
phys-org.description: More people are turning to artificial intelligence (AI)-powered chatbots for companionship and to address loneliness. But can AI-generated empathy replace human connection?

phys-org.title: Chemists develop AI tool to convert human ingenuity into life-enhancing enzymes
phys-org.description: Many have voiced concerns that artificial intelligence will take jobs away from humans. But assistant professor of chemistry Zhongyue (John) Yang, along with his former doctoral student Qianzhen Shao (now a postdoc at Stanford) and other team members, has created an AI tool that aims to elevate the work that scientists do—not replace them.

undark.title: Body Snatchers and the Murky Process of Whole-Body Donation
undark.description: Opinion | Each year, more than 20,000 people in the U.S. donate their bodies to science after death. But the programs that handle whole-body donations lack oversight, with inconsistencies in standards of consent, transparency, and accountability. The result is reminiscent of the body-snatching practices of years past.

undark.title: Book Review: The Bizarre Frontiers of Product Testing
undark.description: From rampaging bears to zero-G toilets and chicken cannons, Alex Davies, in “Kobuk the Destroyer,” chronicles the surprising and often bizarre world of test engineering, and the ingenious lengths to which product testers will go to make the world a safer place.

undark.title: After Cancer, a Complex Aftermath for Survivors
undark.description: Around 70 percent of people with cancer today will live for more than five years after their diagnosis. They’re likely to find that life after cancer is complicated — marked by health risks and chronic illnesses — and that their primary care doctors may be ill-equipped to help them navigate it.

undark.title: Could an Amazonian Highway Open a Pandora’s Box of Pathogens?
undark.description: Brazil has plans to repave a neglected 550-mile road in the South American rainforest to help connect the region and boost economic growth. But some scientists are concerned the project — which would likely increase access between humans, livestock, and wildlife — might be a biosecurity risk.

undark.title: Interview: The Nerve That Could Transform Medicine
undark.description: Kevin Tracey, a researcher and neurosurgeon whose team discovered the vagus nerve’s link to the immune system more than two decades ago, has developed an electrical implant to stimulate the nerve in an effort to help rheumatoid arthritis sufferers who currently have difficulty taking medications.

undark.title: AI and Virtual Reality Enter the Therapist’s Office
undark.description: Some experts say that deepfake technology and other AI tools could help tackle treatment-resistant conditions like anorexia and prolonged grief. But plenty of questions remain, including whether there could be damaging side effects and whether the therapy is even effective.

undark.title: On the Weather Radar: Cloudy With a Chance of Birds
undark.description: This year’s spring migration in North America unveiled real-time measures at a higher resolution than ever before. On one night, for instance, 156 million birds appeared in the skies, outpacing the forecasted total by 20 million. And researchers figured that out thanks to AI.

undark.title: In a Long-Awaited Move, FDA Enforces Trial Result Transparency
undark.description: After years of limited oversight, the FDA sent warnings to more than 2,200 clinical trial sponsors about missing results, which were supposed to be uploaded to an official public database. Experts have pushed for greater transparency.

undark.title: Book Review: An Optimistic Defense of Uncertainty in Science
undark.description: At an uncertain moment in the sciences, Stuart Firestein argues in favor of optimism in “It Could Be Otherwise,” since uncertainty leaves room for possibility, and possibility drives curiosity, imagination, and the agency to study the peculiarities of the natural world.

undark.title: The New Importance of the Scientific Seminar
undark.description: Opinion | The rise of artificial intelligence in science complicates the notion of expertise. When AI can be used to generate ideas, conduct research, and write papers, live scientific presentations — such as public talks and seminars — become more important as a way to demonstrate who is a real expert and who is not.

proj-syn.title: The Politics of Poland’s Judicial Crisis
proj-syn.description: The removal of Bogdan Święczkowski as president of the Constitutional Tribunal has triggered a physical confrontation at the court and a political standoff between Donald Tusk’s government and the far-right Law and Justice (PiS) party. But Święczkowski was not so much removed as barred, because he held the position illegally.

proj-syn.title: Mapping AI Resistance
proj-syn.description: Since a society that is reluctant to deploy a technology will not capture its gains, it is worth understanding why the AI revolution is being welcomed in some places and resisted in others. The explanation is not as simple as headline poll data and much media coverage suggest.

proj-syn.title: The World’s Perilous Ebola Complacency
proj-syn.description: The exponential trajectory of the latest Ebola outbreak is an urgent reminder that infectious diseases do not wait for ideal geopolitical alignments or balanced budgets. Global leaders must fund the Africa-led regional response today, or risk paying an immeasurably higher price in human lives and economic devastation tomorrow.

proj-syn.title: Industrial Decarbonization Is Good for Business
proj-syn.description: With major governments showing open hostility toward climate solutions or focusing on other needs, one might think that progress toward decarbonization is in jeopardy. Yet across the global industrial sector, many companies are increasing productivity, boosting revenue growth, and reducing emissions all at once.

proj-syn.title: When the AI Bubble Bursts
proj-syn.description: Speculative bubbles often leave behind valuable infrastructure while bankrupting the investors who financed them. AI could follow the same path, but the industry’s growing reliance on borrowed money raises the risk of a major financial crisis long before its world-beating applications emerge.

proj-syn.title: After Brazil and Serbia’s Elections
proj-syn.description: The recent electoral defeat of far-right forces in Brazil and Serbia offers important lessons for pro-democracy forces around the world as they confront nationalist and illiberal movements. But no single election can guarantee democracy’s resilience, and the challenges these countries’ new governments face remain formidable.

proj-syn.title: The New Geopolitics of Mining
proj-syn.description: While the US and China want their critical-mineral investments to deliver the biggest returns possible, governments in resource-rich countries must balance external pressures with internal demands. Mining firms must also win local communities’ trust, as host countries will be quick to throw them under the bus if public opinion sours.

proj-syn.title: Can Bond Vigilantes Prevent the Next Debt Crisis?
proj-syn.description: With interest rates on government debt having gone from near zero to much higher levels in recent years, rising short- and long-term bond yields have cast doubt on the sustainability of some debts and led many to wonder if a crisis might be looming. While some countries are more protected than others, none is immune.

proj-syn.title: A Wealth Tax Would Harm California
proj-syn.description: Before approving a one-time tax on the wealth of billionaires who lived in the state at a certain point in time, Californians should consider what such a policy will do to future tax revenues. Since wealth is mobile, those who stand to lose the most will simply leave, taking their future income-tax payments with them.

proj-syn.title: A Future for Europe’s Youth
proj-syn.description: The current generation of young Europeans possesses freedoms, material resources, opportunities to travel, and technological capabilities beyond anything previous generations could have imagined. Their demands, however, are strikingly simple: decent schools, secure jobs, affordable homes, and the possibility of raising a family.

proj-syn.title: A Tale of Two Chinas
proj-syn.description: China’s economy is deeply unbalanced, with a battered real-estate sector, weak consumption, and stark regional disparities coexisting with dynamic tech and export sectors. But provided that political stability is maintained, China could continue to be a global powerhouse even as hundreds of millions of its citizens remain poor.

proj-syn.title: Sino–American Stability?
proj-syn.description: Delegates at the Bund Summit in Shanghai largely agreed that the US-China relationship could be entering a new, less contentious chapter, although many were more interested in what the post-Trump era will mean for Sino-American ties. But perhaps the most heartening sign for the future was the honest exchange of views.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Winter of Discontent
proj-syn.description: Although it is true that European integration has always been forged through crisis, the continent’s postwar story was largely one of incremental responses to relatively manageable challenges. Today, the European Union is facing multiple, interrelated problems that challenge its very raison d’être.

proj-syn.title: How Students Dethroned Serbia’s Strongman
proj-syn.description: Following the ouster of Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán after 16 years in power earlier this year, the world has once again witnessed the merits of “old-school” campaigning. In toppling their own country's strongman, Serbia's new student-led opposition offers important lessons for those defending democracy elsewhere.

proj-syn.title: What a US-China AI Safety Channel Needs
proj-syn.description: Addressing AI safety risks depends on close collaboration between the two leading AI powers, and the establishment of an incident-reporting channel is just a small step in this direction. But success will require that the US and Chinese governments actually understand what is happening under their own noses.

proj-syn.title: The Authoritarian Logic of Selective Privacy
proj-syn.description: Around the world, governments are increasingly deciding who gets privacy and who is denied it, a double standard that turns a fundamental democratic right into a privilege. US President Donald Trump’s administration is a prime example, shielding ICE agents from scrutiny while expanding surveillance of immigrants and protesters.

proj-syn.title: Brazil’s Chapter in the Anti-Authoritarian Playbook
proj-syn.description: Brazil’s renewed democratic confidence must now be matched by institutional and structural reforms and a willingness to build coalitions beyond the left. Recent democratic outcomes in Hungary and Serbia offer useful lessons.

crunchbase.description: Numeracle, a McLean, Virginia-based company that verifies businesses and links their identities to the phone numbers they use to contact customers, has raised $28 million from Edison Partners to help businesses whose calls are incorrectly labeled as spam or blocked by phone carriers.

crunchbase.title: The Invisible Graph: How Companies Grow Revenue And Still Lose Value
crunchbase.description: Revenue growth does not guarantee a larger exit, as declining valuation multiples can outweigh operating gains and reduce enterprise value. Guest author Itay Sagie suggests that founders and boards should track valuation alongside financial performance, model the effects of delaying a sale, and begin M&A preparation while the business is strong and buyer interest is favorable.

crunchbase.title: From Monk To Startups: One Founder’s Unusual Path To Building Government Software
crunchbase.description: After living as a monk while managing Graves’ disease, a former Facebook engineer left Big Tech to pursue meaningful work, eventually founding government software startup FSH Technologies which aims to improve processes such as school food services and public records management through the use of artificial intelligence.

crunchbase.title: Crunchbase Data Shows Q3 Robotics Startup Funding Jumps 185% As US And China Lead Physical AI Push
crunchbase.description: Venture funding to robotics startups has soared in 2026, with the bulk of investment going to companies based in China and the U.S., Crunchbase data shows. All told, global venture funding to robotics startups totaled $9.9 billion in Q3, more than double the $4.3 billion invested in Q3 2025, per Crunchbase data.

crunchbase.title: Your AI Agents Need A Chief Operating Officer, Too
crunchbase.description: Scaling AI agents requires treating them like employees in regulated roles, with written rules, clearly defined responsibilities and a named human manager accountable for their performance. Guest author Rick Folgmann, COO at Get Covered, tells companies they should start with tasks governed by established rules, adjust autonomy to each workflow’s risks, and regularly review results before expanding agents’ authority.
